EXECUTIVE SUMMARY
The Middle East is experiencing severe military escalation, marked by intense, multi-day US strikes across southern Iran and direct Iranian retaliation against US bases in Jordan, Bahrain, and Kuwait. This heightened conflict has extended to commercial shipping, with Iranian missiles hitting two Emirati tankers in the Strait of Hormuz, leading to reports of shipping being almost completely halted and a dramatic surge in oil prices. The US has declared itself the "Guardian of the Hormuz Strait," announcing a 20% toll on all cargo and a naval blockade on Iran, further exacerbating an already volatile situation.

IRAN
Military operations in and against Iran have significantly escalated. The US Central Command (CENTCOM) announced the completion of its latest wave of strikes at 10:15 PM ET on July 13 (02:15 UTC, July 14), which lasted five hours and targeted military objectives across southern Iran, including Bushehr, Chabahar, Jask, Konarak, Abu Musa, and Bandar Abbas. These strikes aimed to degrade Iran's ability to attack commercial shipping, employing precision munitions against Iranian coastal defense systems, missile and UAV sites, and naval capabilities. Specific attacks were reported on Kish Island (targeting the commercial port and boat maintenance facilities), Jam (Chaman base), Saravan (IRGC HQ and airport), Mahshahr, Omidiyeh (a suspected tunnel missile site), and Bandar Lengeh. CENTCOM confirmed the first-time use of 'Corsair' unmanned surface vessels (USVs) in combat, targeting a submarine and ship maintenance facility in Bandar Abbas.

In retaliation, Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) claimed ballistic missile strikes on a US airbase in Jordan (Muwaffaq Salti Air Base), asserting it was used for attacks against Iran. Jordan's military confirmed intercepting four missiles launched from Iran, with no casualties or material damage. The IRGC also claimed missile and drone attacks on the US Fifth Fleet Headquarters in Bahrain's Juffair base, stating they destroyed a Patriot radar, air control radar, C-RAM early warning radar, fuel depots, and an unmanned surface vessel control center. Bahrain's Ministry of Interior confirmed siren activations and explosions, with reports of banking system disruptions attributed to a cyberattack. The Iranian Army announced separate drone attacks on US military communications systems, fuel depots, a Patriot system, a control tower, and an ammunition depot in Kuwait, and a cruise missile strike on a "hostile US vessel." Kuwait reported explosions.

In the Strait of Hormuz, the IRGC claimed to have struck and disabled two "super oil tankers" that allegedly ignored warnings and navigated through a "mined route." The UAE Ministry of Defense identified these as Emirati-flagged "Mombasa" and "Al-Bahiyah" and reported they were hit by two Iranian cruise missiles in Omani territorial waters. One Indian crew member was killed, and eight others were injured, four critically. The UK Maritime Trade Operations (UKMTO) reported an incident involving a tanker 40 nautical miles northeast of Qalhat, Oman. Bloomberg reported that shipping through the Strait of Hormuz had almost completely halted early on Tuesday. Iran also announced it shot down a US MQ-1 drone over the Strait of Hormuz.

Internally, The New York Times reported on a multi-year Mossad operation to cultivate former Iranian President Mahmoud Ahmadinejad as a potential leader for a post-regime Iran, including meetings with former Mossad chief Dadi Barnea in Budapest. The report claimed an Israeli strike on Ahmadinejad’s compound on February 28 was followed by a Mossad extraction to a secret safe house in Iran. Ahmadinejad reportedly left the safe house and is now under house arrest by the IRGC Intelligence Organization after his ties to Israel were discovered. The Iranian Parliament, after months of closure, held its first public session on July 13, focusing on "revenge for the killers" of former Leader Ali Khamenei. Brent crude prices surged to over $85 a barrel amidst the escalating tensions. Iranian Foreign Minister Seyed Abbas Araghchi responded to Trump's proposed 20% toll in the Strait of Hormuz, asserting Iran's role as the "eternal guardian" but deeming the 20% fee "too much" and promising to be "fair."

ISRAEL
Israeli military operations included preventing settler activists, calling themselves the Bashan Pioneers, from illegally crossing the border into Syria in the southern Golan Heights. The IDF condemned these actions as criminal and disruptive. The IDF also concluded five months of "intense activity" in Lebanon by the Givati brigade, involving operations beyond the Litani River and significant engagement in Bint Jbeil. In the Gaza Strip, the IDF announced the killing of Mustafa Owaisi, a Palestinian weapons smuggler, in an airstrike in southern Gaza on July 13, stating he was attempting to rebuild Hamas's military wing in violation of a ceasefire.

On the home front, six fragmentation grenades were thrown across Israel, including in Nes Ziona, two incidents in Tel Aviv, and two at Japanika restaurant branches in Afula and Netanya. Police suspect these are linked to a criminal conflict between two families, targeting businesses owned by Barak Abramov. Casualties included two Bezeq employees injured by stones in Kifl Haris who refused hospitalization, a 74-year-old woman seriously injured in Kfar Sulum, two men moderately injured in a traffic accident near Gan Hadarom, a 3-year-old boy in serious condition from drowning in Tel Sheva, and an 80-year-old woman who drowned in Michmoret.

Politically, the Knesset approved the controversial "Torah Study Basic Law" by a vote of 63 to 52, which exempts yeshiva students from military conscription. This triggered widespread condemnation from opposition leaders (Yair Lapid, Gadi Eisenkot, Naftali Bennett, Avigdor Lieberman, Yair Golan, Chili Tropper, Yoaz Hendel), with former PM Bennett labeling the government "the most anti-Zionist in Israeli history." The IDF Chief of Staff warned that the law would incentivize non-compliance and harm the reserve system. Coalition infighting continued, with United Torah Judaism leader Moshe Gafni threatening to halt all legislative votes until an arrest deferral law is passed for draft evaders. Prime Minister Netanyahu and faction leader Haim Katz reached a compromise on Likud primaries, reserving eight spots for Netanyahu. The security cabinet is scheduled to convene on July 15 at 20:00.

In other developments, an indictment against Reut Ben Haim for blocking aid to Gaza was reversed following public outcry. Settlement expansion continued, with the first caravan neighborhood placed in Ganim in northern Samaria, 20 years after its evacuation.

GAZA & WEST BANK
Israeli forces conducted airstrikes in the southern Gaza Strip, targeting areas in Rafah and Khan Yunis, and also struck near the Al-Zweida refugee camp in central Gaza. The IDF killed Mustafa Owaisi, a Palestinian weapons smuggler, in southern Gaza yesterday (July 13), who was accused of rebuilding Hamas's military wing in violation of a ceasefire agreement.

The humanitarian situation is deteriorating, with the Coordinator of Government Activities in the Territories (COGAT) reporting that Hamas militants forcibly seized a World Food Programme (WFP) food distribution compound in Jabalia, assaulted two truck drivers, and confiscated the food warehouse. This action has halted food distribution to thousands of families, with COGAT condemning Hamas for exploiting humanitarian aid.

In the West Bank, Hamas criticized Israel's decision to grant city status to the illegal Giv'at Ze'ev settlement northwest of occupied al-Quds.

LEBANON
The IDF's Givati brigade completed five months of "intense activity" in Lebanon, which included operations beyond the Litani River and a significant engagement in Bint Jbeil. Israeli strikes "deep in Lebanon" were reported as explosions were heard in the Western Galilee. Press TV alleged that Israel is using white phosphorus in southern Lebanon, causing fires in villages and farmlands, and demolishing homes, despite a US-mediated framework agreement. Lebanese Army helicopters were observed flying over Beirut and its southern suburbs shortly before sunrise.

SYRIA & IRAQ
Iran launched a missile attack against a camp of Iranian-Kurdish opposition forces in northern Iraq, near Erbil. A US airbase in Jordan (Muwaffaq Salti Air Base) was targeted by Iranian ballistic missiles, with Jordanian authorities confirming the interception of four missiles. Saudi Arabia conducted airstrikes on Yemen's Sa'ada Governorate. On the Israeli border, Israeli settler activists attempted to illegally cross into Syrian territory from the southern Golan Heights, but were intercepted and detained by IDF forces.

GULF STATES
The Gulf States are deeply embroiled in the escalating regional conflict.
**Bahrain** experienced repeated siren activations and significant explosions. The IRGC claimed missile and drone strikes targeted the US Fifth Fleet Headquarters in Juffair, hitting a Patriot radar, air control radar, C-RAM early warning radar, fuel depots, and the control center for unmanned surface vessels. Bahrain's Ministry of Interior urged citizens and residents to seek safe locations. Reports indicated disruptions to Bahrain's banking systems following a cyberattack.
**Kuwait** also reported explosions. The Iranian Army claimed its drones targeted US military communications systems, fuel depots, a Patriot system, a control tower, and an ammunition depot in Kuwait.
The **United Arab Emirates (UAE)** Ministry of Defense reported that two Emirati oil tankers, "Mombasa" and "Al-Bahiyah," were hit by two Iranian cruise missiles in Omani territorial waters, south of the Strait of Hormuz shipping lane. One Indian crew member was killed, and eight others were injured, four critically. Explosions were reported in Abu Dhabi. The US Embassy in Abu Dhabi and the US Consulate in Dubai canceled all consular appointments from July 13-15 due to the regional security situation, and US non-emergency government personnel remain under "mandatory evacuation." The UAE Foreign Ministry condemned the attacks on commercial shipping as "piracy" and called for the unconditional reopening of the Strait of Hormuz. DP World is reportedly developing a new multipurpose port in Fujairah to bypass the Strait of Hormuz.
**Saudi Arabia** received President Trump's approval and support for military action against the Houthis in Yemen. It subsequently launched airstrikes on Sana'a International Airport, reportedly to prevent an Iranian plane from landing. This prompted Houthi retaliation with ballistic missile and drone attacks on Abha International Airport in southern Saudi Arabia. The Houthi military spokesman warned all airlines to avoid Saudi airspace until the blockade on Sana'a International Airport is lifted. Press TV reported that Saudi Arabia is willing to resume Abraham Accords talks with the US, conditional on Benjamin Netanyahu's replacement as Israeli Prime Minister and reversal of certain West Bank decisions.
**Oman's** Foreign Minister, Bader Al-Busaidi, criticized past "containment and isolation" policies towards Iran, stating that the recent war proved their failure to achieve regional security and stability.

The **Strait of Hormuz** has become a central flashpoint. President Trump declared the US as the "Guardian of the Hormuz Strait," announcing a 20% toll on all cargo passing through for security costs, and reinstating a naval blockade on Iran that would prevent Iranian ships or clients from using the Strait. Iranian Foreign Minister Araghchi countered that Iran is the "eternal guardian" and that 20% is "too much," but Iran would be "fair." Shipping in the Strait of Hormuz was reportedly almost completely halted.

KEY DEVELOPMENTS
1.  **Intensified US-Iran Military Conflict**: US CENTCOM concluded a five-hour strike wave across multiple Iranian locations (Bushehr, Chabahar, Jask, Konarak, Abu Musa, Bandar Abbas, Kish, Qeshm, Jam, Saravan, Mahshahr, Omidiyeh, Bandar Lengeh) using precision munitions and, for the first time, 'Corsair' unmanned surface vessels (USVs).
2.  **Widespread Iranian Retaliation**: Iran's IRGC claimed missile/drone strikes on US military assets in Bahrain (Fifth Fleet HQ Juffair, Patriot/C-RAM radars, fuel depots) and a US airbase in Jordan (Muwaffaq Salti Air Base), with Jordan confirming four intercepts. The Iranian Army also claimed drone/cruise missile strikes on US military assets in Kuwait and a hostile US vessel.
3.  **Attack on Emirati Tankers in Strait of Hormuz**: Two Emirati oil tankers, "Mombasa" and "Al-Bahiyah," were hit by two Iranian cruise missiles in Omani territorial waters, killing one Indian crew member and injuring eight others. This incident contributed to reports of shipping in the Strait of Hormuz being almost completely halted.
4.  **US Declares "Guardian of Hormuz Strait" and 20% Toll**: President Trump announced the reinstatement of a naval blockade on Iran and declared the US as the "Guardian of the Hormuz Strait," imposing a 20% toll on all cargo passing through for security costs.
5.  **UK Designates IRGC as Terrorist Organization**: The British government officially proscribed Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) as a terrorist organization, making membership or support a criminal offense.
6.  **Saudi-Houthi Escalation in Yemen**: Saudi Arabia launched airstrikes on Sana'a International Airport, prompting Houthi retaliation with ballistic missile and drone attacks on Abha International Airport in Saudi Arabia. This escalation follows US approval for Saudi military action against the Houthis.
7.  **"Torah Study Basic Law" Passed in Israel**: The Knesset approved the controversial "Torah Study Basic Law" (63-52), which exempts yeshiva students from military conscription, drawing strong condemnation from opposition parties and warnings from the IDF Chief of Staff regarding its negative impact on the military.
8.  **Mossad Plot to Install Ahmadinejad Revealed**: The New York Times reported that Israel's Mossad had a years-long plan to cultivate former Iranian President Mahmoud Ahmadinejad as a potential leader of a post-regime Iran, including meetings with ex-Mossad chief Barnea and an attempted extraction during the current conflict. Ahmadinejad is now reportedly under IRGC house arrest.

THREAT ASSESSMENT
Escalation risks are extremely high, with direct military confrontation between the US and Iran intensifying. Both sides are engaging in strikes on sovereign territory and naval assets, crossing previously established red lines. The US declaration of itself as the "Guardian of the Hormuz Strait" and its imposition of a 20% toll, coupled with Iranian threats to retaliate and close Bab al-Mandab, represents a severe escalation that could trigger a global energy crisis. The reported halting of shipping in the Strait of Hormuz is a critical flashpoint, indicating potential for significant economic and military consequences.

Active flashpoints include the Strait of Hormuz (naval clashes, drone shootdowns, tanker attacks, US blockade/toll), Bahrain (US bases targeted), Kuwait (US bases targeted), Jordan (US airbase targeted), and southern Iran (multiple US strikes). The Yemen/Saudi border also remains highly volatile due to ongoing Houthi-Saudi exchanges.

Military postures are shifting, with the US increasing its presence (50,000 troops in the Middle East) and deploying advanced weapons, such as unmanned surface vessels, for sustained multi-day strikes. Iran is actively retaliating against US bases in Gulf states and Jordan, demonstrating a willingness to engage beyond its borders. Israel has placed all its military pilots on 100% standby, indicating a high state of alert.

REGIONAL & INTERNATIONAL RESPONSE
The **US** posture, articulated by President Trump, includes confirmation of renewed "limited, measured, and planned" military operations against Iran for a third consecutive night, targeting capabilities related to the Strait of Hormuz. Trump announced the US would act as the "Guardian of the Hormuz Strait," imposing a 20% toll on cargo and reinstating a naval blockade on Iran, and stated he would seek compensation from Gulf States for security efforts. He also approved Saudi Arabia's military actions against the Houthis.

Among the **Gulf States**, the UAE Ministry of Defense condemned Iranian attacks on its tankers, calling for the unconditional reopening of Hormuz and labeling commercial shipping attacks as "piracy." Saudi Arabia, with US backing, conducted strikes on Sana'a. Bahrain reported multiple siren activations and explosions at US bases, with its Ministry of Interior urging residents to take cover. Kuwait reported explosions at US bases. Oman's Foreign Minister, Bader Al-Busaidi, publicly criticized past "containment and isolation of Iran" policies, declaring them a failure.

**EU members** showed division regarding Israeli settlements, with less than half of foreign ministers supporting concrete steps to curtail trade. The **United Kingdom** officially designated Iran's IRGC as a terrorist organization.

**Russia**, through its UN envoy, stated that Iran's flight to Sana'a was "humanitarian," countering US claims of military personnel transport.

**Brazil's** President Lula da Silva condemned the US plan to charge transit fees in Hormuz as "piracy" and warned that US attacks on Iran could lead to price hikes for essential goods.

**Ukraine** and President Trump reached a deal for Ukraine to receive licenses to produce Patriot systems. Ukraine also formed a ballistic missile defense coalition with nine European countries.

INTELLIGENCE NOTES
Several aspects of the reporting require careful consideration due to contradictions, unverified claims, and potential propaganda. Attributions of retaliatory strikes sometimes vary between "Iran," "IRGC," and "Iranian Army," although official announcements later clarify.

There are conflicting reports on the extent of casualties and damage. While the IRGC claims to have "destroyed" US Patriot radars, air control systems, C-RAM, fuel depots, and USV control centers in Bahrain, and to have "demolished" a US airbase in Kuwait, US CENTCOM has not detailed damage to its own assets. Jordan confirmed intercepting missiles, not direct hits, which implies limited impact. President Trump's unverified claims that Ali Khamenei is dead and his son, Mojtaba Khamenei, is "90% gone" are highly speculative and not supported by independent evidence. Similarly, Trump's assertions of 52,000 Iranians killed by the regime and 230 Iranian planes hit lack independent confirmation.

Reporting gaps include a lack of independent verification for specific Iranian claims of military success against US targets in Bahrain, Kuwait, and Jordan. Comprehensive damage assessments from US strikes within Iran, beyond general target categories, are also limited in open sources. The precise economic impact and the full extent of the reported halting of shipping in the Strait of Hormuz are currently unclear.

Propaganda indicators are prevalent across all involved parties. IRGC messages, particularly those addressing "Noble and Muslim people of Jordan" with religious overtones ("Yatharath al-Hussein"), appear designed to foster regional solidarity against the US. President Trump's assertive statements about "hitting them hard" and "taking everything from Iran" also serve a rhetorical and morale-boosting function. Houthi communications frequently include explicit anti-US and anti-Israel slogans.

Unverified claims include reports of banking system disruptions in Bahrain due to a cyberattack, and local messages of power outages in Jask after an explosion. Numerous reports from various Iranian cities (Tabriz, Kermanshah, Orumiyeh, Mashhad, Nayshabur, Sirjan) of explosions or sounds of explosions, often from local, unverified sources, indicate widespread apprehension but require independent corroboration for specific impacts.
